Population increased in Manchester

The estimated population of Manchester in 2024 was 589,670 usual residents, a rise of 1.4% since 2023.

This meant that Manchester's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Manchester increased by 7.1%.

Over this slightly longer period, Manchester was also among the 10% fastest growing local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Manchester

The average (median) age fell to 30.4 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Manchester has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Manchester is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Manchester's population of 589,670 usual residents was made up of:

  • 116,876 people aged 0 to 15 years, (19.8%)
  • 417,700 people aged 16 to 64 years, (70.8%)
  • 55,094 people aged 65 years and over, (9.3%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Manchester has a lower proportion of people aged 65 years and over (9.3% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Manchester, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Manchester
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Manchester, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More births than deaths increased the population of 3,038 people (0.5%). In total, there were 6,634 births and 3,596 deaths in Manchester.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) led to a fall in the population of 11,253 (-1.9%). There were 57,369 people entering the area and 68,622 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Manchester's population of 16,620 (2.9%) as a result of 26,229 people entering the area and 9,609 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Manchester was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Manchester in mid-2023 is 581,302.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 1,410 people and internal migration estimates were revised downwards by 25 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 1,385 people.
